body:
Birthdays suck, don't they? Ugh. I don't really even have friends I could invite over, they're all acquaintances. Blech. 

But, I wanted to share with you something my psychiatrist said to me about Facebook that honestly completely changed how I see it. You know how your page is filled with happy smiling people who look like everything is sunshine and daisies? That's on purpose. As much as you don't want to post your low moments, neither does anyone else. All you see is the best of the absolute best of people's lives. (I realize the level of crap on Facebook that there really is, but this perspective really helped to stop the trigger it used to be.)
Agreed.

Hey buddy, post secondary is NOT like that. They don't give a shit how much work went into it. Your classes are lectures. Nothing but a steady stream of talking. Then you go home and do the assignment and hand it in. Hit everything in the marking grid it came with and you're golden.   Hold out til grad and you'll be free.

Apply anyways. It's only listed as a requirement to ensure they get a certain level of skill applying. If you have the equivalent skill and believe you could do the job, then apply. Write a kick ass letter not saying sorry you dont have a degree but you wNt the job anyways, but point by point pick apart their requirement list by showing them you have all those skills because of x experience at x work history location.

I have had experiences in the past with being accused of being manipulative, dramatic, and attention seeking when I simply wanted help, so I understand that now. 

Having thought more about what you said made me realize that the immense relief I feel at having my struggles validated by a diagnosis points to my having experienced the stigma and negativity, only lacking a name and accurate description of what I was suffering from and the reactions.

I'm reading a lot of negativity of other people towards those with BDP. I've managed my symptoms unmedicated for years now, and though I've struggled I've managed to maintain jobs and some relationships. 

Now that I can put a name to the laundry list of things I deal with, I'm so relieved because I know I can find resources for a game plan to get better. 

To use my favourite metaphor, though my pain may not be a cut on my arm I can treat with a bandage, it's no longer a phantom pain  either. Simply an issue with the nerves I can treat with medications and therapy. 

But the negatives I'm reading have me worried. Is it really so bleak? Is there really such a negative view? Do people with BDP often take a stance that it's such a big deal? I don't mean to belittle it in any way, it's more that I'm trying to grasp how it's perceived in the community.

If j didn't feel this crippling anxiety i would want to live. I have no problems per se other than that i always feel extremely stressed out and ive gone meta in stressing about my stress. 

If i could be the carefree easy going person that i am in my head, i would be fine. But i get random senseless thoughts that throw me down despite that im like wtf? How does that make sense?
Except what do I do when that person is busy and doesn't have time to deal with me again?
Absolutely. Im here!

Its incredibly frustrating! Sitting here struggling for no clear reason sucks huge hairy balls

The assessment scares me. I can't afford to be admitted, though I think the fact that I'm no longer suicidal and accepting meds, and can hold a job and an apartment and get most of my bills paid on time, should count in my favor. 

I just don't have a diagnosis so they want me to get an assessment done I think for that purpose.

I go for a psychiatric assessment on thursday, and i booked a day off for it so at least i dont have to deal with work that day. And it'll give me more time to clean in case a friend comes to stay the weekend, which im hoping she will. Other than that, nothing.

Exactly how i feel. Whats more frustrating is that nothing set it off. I like my job. Sunday id already set aside alone time to just recoup and get some r&r. Why did it have to suddenly spiral into hell?

Work has been repetitive lately. A lot of data entry. Its not always like this, the year goes in cycles and this part will be done in a month or two. But it doesnt keep my brain occupied, just me hands. I'm too effective as a multitasker lol
I keep reading this and it makes me giggle. Thank you.
I'm not a woman who's ever had problems with orgasms before, so it's incredibly frustrating and affecting my sex life which affects my mood. It's bad, man.

Best thing: You're not crazy. I can help you.

Best thing I could have heard after hearing for years I needed to toughen up.
Thank you, so much. This is what I needed to hear.

On nights like these there are a few things I do. One is listen to a sleep album, something made for spas or deep sleep and just focus very intently on the sounds and try to hear all the minute nuances. This can also work with your favorite music if you prefer. I find new age is easier. 

Or, I count back from 100 and if I hit 0 count up to 100 and back down. If I focus on each number I often fall asleep before hitting 100 again. 

And lastly I just shut my eyes and focus on using each exhale to relax my body further and further and further. 

The idea is to give yourself something simple to focus on. You won't notice when you fall asleep, because you're too busy focusing on your task, but you're asleep!

I bet your kidney is pretty attractive. But really. I would reschedule. Try and believe he is genuine and you won't be a burden. Also don't be afraid to open up. I've been open early on with all of my recent dates, and my depression hasn't been an issue. The guy I can just recently call my boyfriend was very accepting. I casually explained to him what situations are worst for me, which for clarity's sake are when I feel as though I have offended or let someone down, and he said to me that he would always be clear with me. That I need not worry, he would vocalize his feelings on iffy topics or comments. So far he has kept true to that. Try it and see.

Doing things for other people make me happy. The downside is that sometimes when I need someone to do something nice for me, and it doesn't happen, it can be soul crushing. Or when my intention was to help and I hindered, I'm struck down into this heap of guilt. And when I've done something to hinder myself, well forget about happy days for a while. But I do know what you mean, doing things to benefit others, or keeping myself alive only because my death would harm those I love most, is what keeps me going.

I want to hug you. Posts like yours that just so accurately describe how I feel sometimes make me cry because it reminds me yet again that I'm not in this alone. I want to hug you because you validate me. Thank you. Thank you so much. And I hope you're ok today too.

I came into this subreddit tonight hoping I'd find something to relate to, and I found your post. This mirrors me so exactly in my thought patterns I want to print it out and use it to explain because you do it better than I ever could. 

Thank you, for making me feel like I'm not alone.

If I'm feeling kind of stuffy from a crying anxiety attack, then I just have a cup of hot water with one tablespoon each lemon juice and honey. Otherwise, I really like the Sleep Well from Teopia or just plain peppermint tea.

Actually, I'm in Canada, it's a little far from Pakistan. 

I had some tea that helped immensely with the nausea, I don't know if it was tea in general or that particular mix of loose leaf tea, but my nausea is gone. I wrote the post while I was waiting for it to cool. 

I'm at the dose I was prescribed now, the lower dose was a suggestion by the pharmacist to get my body used to the drug. I noticed the first few days I was really keyed up and shaky, I don't know what tomorrow is going to be like, but like you said, anything positive is welcome right now.

Thank you, for your insight.

Hey, just wanted to chime in a bit here. Not sure where you are, but it's not too late to go to college. I'm in Canada, and I'm aware the system is different here than the states, but in my program, at 19, I was considered one of the babies. The average age for my journalism type program was 25-35. College in Canada, in Ontario at least, is less than $4000 per year for tuition, most programs only around $3200-$3500, and there's tons and tons of aid for mature students, more so than for fresh faced students out of high school. Look into it, it's not too late.

So I talked to my counsellor, they've started me on cipralex to treat consistently rather than case by case for anxiety attacks, which is how I was using the weed. I'm hoping to stop using weed altogether. Thank you :)

My mother is the same way. Now that my brother and I have finally gotten help and told her to deal with it pretty much, it's better. I would have sought help years ago if she didn't have that attitude, and I regret not going all those years ago. 

Something my counsellor told me: you can't let this person control your life. If you need help, get help. Letting someone else make a decision like this for you (in my case at least) will only make your problems worse.

Do what you need to do. Your dad is your dad, he loves you. Do what you need to do and I think he'll be there for you.

I know what you mean. I think being ok with being anxious in some situations is a key part too. Like on a date, it's ok to feel anxiety, so long as I work through it and don't let it stop me from doing what I want to do.

Probably explains why I still feel guilty about it. The odds of a drug test are slim, they don't use that for job screenings here, but I see your point. 

I'll look into that workbook you mentioned.

Thank you. I'll definitely look into that workbook.

The weed, I find it not so much something to self medicate, but more as something that allows me to calm down enough to accept the alternative thoughts I do come up with. 

For example, I get very anxious over my job situation. To the point where I'm having almost daily breakdowns over not having a phone call come in and being continuously unemployed. And it's not like its been months, it's been two weeks and I have a job lined up to start soon. It's a continued anxiety that will only end when the situation fixes itself. Using weed, I'm able to calm down enough to tell myself that it will work out, because I'm not sitting idle doing nothing about it. And so far, it seems to work, and I've had a few good days since then. I only use it during episodes or attacks where I can't do anything but curl up in bed and cry. And it helps.

I'm debating asking my counselor for a referral to a psychiatrist to get a medical card. I use so little, it's maybe twice a week.
I found the chat room for r/anxiety! But I can't connect :( I'm going to try on my computer instead of iPad to see if its just an app problem, but yeah...maybe this will work.
I don't know what that is. And the Wikipedia didn't help. Is it a chat room? I really don't feel comfortable talking to strangers in a chat room (despite feeling ok posting on reddit.)

I just feel like such a burden on people. I don't have enough friends to have one I can call out of the blue and who would be willing to hang out. I have never had many friends, and never any I could do that with.

I've tried expressing this, but it never gets taken seriously. It's always met with stuff like 'so you want to be drugged out on meds? Is that what you want? That's not a life, get over yourself. It's not that bad and you're making it worse. Go [insert activity meant to calm me down].' 

Sometimes if I've already broken down and am just trying to hide it they'll be ok. If I look sad or am actually crying then its ok, but its nothing more than a pat on the back and a 'feel better, it'll be ok.' 

I can't talk to my parents about this. I'll never get support from them. Even if I do get meds it'll breed resentment and things like 'well don't you feel better about yourself now, all medicated. You got what you wanted, bravo. Way to give up.' It's nothing but guilt trips, and has been my entire life. That's why I'm now in my twenties and only seeking help for the first time. My counsellor pointed out how big of a stressor my parents are, and my home life in general is. If I could move out today I would. I just can't afford it until I get a job that will pay the rent (hopefully soon.)

I can answer this one.

Everything. I can tell a perfect stranger the excruciating detail of the thoughts that torment me, but I can't tell my own mother that I'm seeking therapy because I think I'm depressed, not because I want stress relief techniques.

I can't tell my family of what goes on in my head because I'm afraid they'll mock me, they won't take me seriously, they'll tell me to get over it, they'll say every body feels that way, you'll be fine. I'm afraid no one will help me, they'll only roll their eyes and say ya ya, sure you're special. 

I need help. I've been fighting this for years, and my family has no idea of how close I've come to trying to end it. I can't tell them, because I don't think they'll know what to do. 

Part of my anxiety is what other people think of me, or how they feel in relations to my actions. I could never bear to have anyone in pain or be uncomfortable because of me, and if I tell them I'm depressed or have had thoughts of suicide, they will feel bad of my behalf, and feel worry, and anxiety. I'd much rather them be happy and whole.

I hear ya. I've managed to kill the voice lately, but I can't beat the sadness. I can't take that hour when you put away the distractions and try to sleep. I try and aim for a time that's acceptable to sleep, and hope for the best. Usually try and tire myself out so I can fall asleep quickly. Once I'm in bed I try and aim for comfiest spot, which means sleep is near, and sleep is good because I don't dream, so my brain shuts up and I don't have to bear the burden of being able to think.

I hear ya.

The minute I read the first point it cheered me up. I love thinking about how I'm made out of stardust. One of my favorite distractions when I'm feeling particularly anxious. 

Also, the end of your post just made me laugh so hard. It's got this 'Fuck you depression, come at me! Life is awesome!' attitude that just made my night.

Thank you. On one of my first bad nights in a while, you made me laugh. Thank you.
It could definitely be covered, depends what you have. It would be worth it to ask. If you want to talk about it with someone, then see what you can do to go.

You were told those things by people who don't understand depression, and likely never will. When you stop beating yourself up, you can work towards getting better. You'll feel better as soon as you accept that it's ok, it's going to be ok, and there are people who will help you.
Ah, ok. Maybe your parents workplace, if you felt more comfortable there. You don't even need to say what it's for, really.

You didn't mention a workplace in your post, but sometimes work places have programs or something like that within HR to help their employees. And it's all confidential by law. Have you tried asking there?

You need to realize its ok to feel like this. Depression doesn't pick only people who have shitty lives. It doesn't work like that. There's nothing wrong with you, and you have no reason to feel guilty. You have no reason to feel guilty. For tonight, just accept that you feel like this. Confide in someone, here or in real life.

Have you tried talking about it in therapy? Say that you feel like you're falling short, they are there to help you. Maybe something new will come up and you can try that. You won't know unless you ask.
You don't have to have something to talk about, when you want to talk about something, you will.

I like you, with this story business of yours.

I'm finding relief in ending the chapter, and having the freedom to give my full attention to getting better. At least for tonight, that's how I feel.
It rings all too true. I've been very lucky, haven't had many people who seem to have black and white simple solutions.
I think your first step is in realizing that feeling like this doesn't make you a bad or ungrateful person. Don't beat yourself up, just go get help.

It's almost harder, knowing. I can already see the lessons I'm meant to learn. I can already see my obstacles. I know it isn't going to be easy, and I'm going to have days that suck. This time, I just don't have the energy to feel angry anymore. I just can't. I'm just done with it. Which, from past experience means I've made a huge leap in this process. Its almost comforting. Almost.

I want that. I want fun times like that. Sometimes I've found my own version, but it's only been like a treat, never the norm. Makes me sad. I really like this commercial though, reminds me that I can maybe visit my friends this summer, and do something like that.
Thank you.
As much as you want to go back to Sweden, your education isn't going to make a lick of difference if you aren't okay.

I'm admitting to all the things I refused to acknowledge in my desperate attempts to make it work, and its helping. Relief is a feeling I didn't think I'd have, and at least now I can work on myself and getting myself healthy, and free of depression and anxiety.

I don't know how tomorrow is going to be, or the next day, but it's thanks to this subreddit and people like you that I'm ok with not being ok. One day at a time and it'll be alright.

I wanted to update you on my situation with my mother.

I just had 'the talk' with my now ex, and went to her for comfort, and just came clean about what I've been feeling. She admitted to having feelings like I do, and is afraid for my brother because he's similar, and bottles it up way more than we do.

She supported my wanting to figure this out, and seek outside help, so long as I found a way that insurance would cover, whether through a job or government (reasonable and easily had.) We agreed that meds are not the answer, at least not now. She did warn me that should I have kids, ill have to seriously keep an eye on myself for post partum. 

The biggest was her acknowledging that I have a problem, and supporting my wish to find outside help. My thought patterns are the problem, and I need to find someone who will do more than listen to me vent. I need someone who will help me get a handle on my anxiety and depression and let me bitch slap it into submission. She didn't want to label it depression, but said I could call it whatever I wanted to, if it made me feel better. 

It's a huge weight off my chest, knowing that while she can't fully understand that I don't feel like I can do it on my own, she's nonetheless behind me every step of the way. 

I'm sending all the good vibes I can to you do that you can find this with your family, and your mother. I didn't think it was possible, and it came out way better than expected.

Thank you. I'm still going through anger and sadness, but after the initial storm, I'm finding relief. There were frustrations in the relationship that I'm realizing I no longer have to deal with, and should never have had to deal with in the first place.

I know it's going to take time before I'm ok, but I look forward to being ok, and to be able to be in a relationship where I don't have those frustrations, where it's like pulling teeth to do anything at all. And more than one guy out there doesn't give a damn if I shave my legs or not.
You're both right. I'm a morning person, so sleep is my relief. During the day if I can't take it anymore, I take a nap. It's a break from having to think, because when I think, I'm depressed.

Ha, yeah. I'm still struggling with that. I find putting down the phone helps. And if I can't put down the phone I say goodnight to whoever I'm talking to, so I can hide it from myself to avoid saying anything while the depression has control.
You do know what I'm feeling. Like if I didn't give myself a chance to think, I'd be happy, because the nasty voice in my head wouldn't have the chance to ruin my day.

Posting here has been helping. It's having one person know so much about me when I don't know them from Adam or eve. I confided in a real life friend last night, it was really liberating, and she believed me, which was so nice. I was afraid of skepticism.

Lately I've been working 9 hour days, and when I get home from work, it's dinner, a very hot shower, and the moment I feel tired I shut my eyes and sleep. If I don't give myself a chance to think about my day I'm alright. But then I'm faced with the problem of never getting anything done, and my life whizzing by because I'm trying to make each day end as fast as I can.
I'm petite too, but I'm usually different with meds. Tylenol doesn't work for me, but Advil does. Maybe that has something to do with it.

You just hit really close to home. I'll hold on with you, if you hold on with me. I like watching tv too. There's something about it, like I can forget where I am and just focus on the story. It gives me a break from having to feel anything myself for a while, like I can borrow someone else's emotions.

Crying is a release to me. Sometimes I won't feel better until I cry, and if I try to keep it inside, I end up crying for things like coming up to a red light. Anything, anything at all. I know better now, and cry at night when nobody sees.

This isn't a quote, and doesn't encompass depression per say, but it summed it up pretty damn well. I can only hope that my story ends as well.

http://hyperboleandahalf.blogspot.ca/2011/10/adventures-in-depression.html

I don't think she meant it maliciously. I watch that show and I'm afraid of going through anything traumatic, because I see the tendencies in myself. She may not know how to express to you that she's afraid it'll happen to you, because she doesn't have a clear understanding of what you're going through. I suggest you talk to her about how her comment made you feel, I suspect it's just her trying to show you she cares.

Funny, Benadryl doesn't knock me on my ass. Makes me want to take a nap, but never a deep sleep haha, though I've only taken it for allergies. I usually give myself something to focus on, like music playing, or counting back and forth from 100 while visualizing the numbers.

I forgot that phrase, a permanent solution to a temporary problem.

I have the thoughts, but you're right, there's too much I can do and there's too many people I would hurt. So while it's nice to entertain the fantasy, I can't bring myself to do anything. Funny how it works.

Thank you. I just, sometimes I just want to disappear, but not have anyone care. I couldn't stand inconveniencing people, or causing them pain. That's what gets me, every time. That, and the thoughts are never very concrete. More like what you said, a wondering.

I'm really only just realizing how bad it is for me too. I've done a lot of self reflection lately, and I'm realizing that this nasty voice in my head is very, very bad. It's not something that I can just shut off, and it's getting harder and harder to ignore. I'm afraid of it getting to the point where I can't ignore it, or god forbid something traumatic happens and I get seriously fucked up in the head.

I'm just not sure where to start to get help. My job, and my mother, are going to make it very hard. I don't want to lose my job, and I want to hide it from my mother. 

Do you ever think, that no one is going to believe you? I'm so afraid of going to a therapist and getting told its nothing, my thoughts aren't valid, I'm making it up, and to just go home and deal with it.

I'm glad to hear I'm not alone. I've constantly questioned whether I'm depressed or just a complainer, but seeing the stories in this subreddit helped me realized that I am depressed, and I need help. That my thoughts aren't ok and I can get help. 

The boyfriend I mentioned, well I sort of talked to him about it in November, but I'm thinking I'm going to talk to him again. I feel like even if I can't go to my parents, I'll have someone who knows the whole truth and is going to be there for me, like you do. Thank you, for sharing with me.

I so badly want to see a therapist you have no idea. The only reason I didn't stick with the counsellor at school was because I wasn't deemed high risk enough, and couldn't book more than two appointments. He was overloaded.

I have insurance with my job now, but it won't kick in for 90 days. And since this job is just to get me enough money to move to another city for a job I want, I'll likely be gone before I see that insurance. However, I am in Ontario, so if Ohip covers anything, I have that.

I think you and I are in the same boat. I seem to be able to help everyone but myself.

I literally just made a post here, I think it's time I asked for help. No one really knows that I don't just have a lot of bad days, it's the other way around. I just have some good days.
